prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; continuous potable water, operator visibility, auto control, manual intervention. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (alias Ironwood): auto start by demand/channel depth; permissives suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; blocked by low channel level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock; lost permissive -> alarm/stop by severity; shall stay unavailable for maintenance release until isolations tagged, verified locally, acknowledged in shift turnover record. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot at cleaning-cycle end to Maintenance Planner (compares rake work vs loading before release); high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (alias Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket on new lot to Lab Technician; dose trim by analyzer feedback/operator targets; deliveries need hose/containment/washdown inspection. North Filter Gallery (alias Cobalt): per-filter turbidity/headloss each scan. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note. Galleries' work keeps filtration capacity; washed filter returns only when rinse-to-waste meets target. Chlorine Contact Basin: Chlorine Residual Alarm; nearby chemical work needs ventilation, gas monitoring, comms. Clearwell Level Controller: buffer; changes coordinated with High Service Pump Header plan. Backwash Recovery Tank: sampled after return-to-process. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (alias Sparrow): sends Jar Test Photograph Set after date/time/ID check. SCADA Historian Server (alias Lantern): retains doses, analyzer values, filter status, washes, comments, lab timestamps for audit. Actors: Chief Operator (modes, targets, doses, next-day schedule review); Duty Engineer (reviews field/lab differences, checks work vs constraints, may defer nonessential work); Maintenance Planner (alias Quarry; work orders list equipment, isolations, parts, closure evidence); Laboratory Technician (custody/condition checks, sends Sample Chain Slip, QC); Distribution Dispatcher (informed before availability changes of High Service Pump Header, North/South Distribution Pressure Station); Chemical Supplier Driver (sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; operator-observed access); Residuals Hauler; auditors; craft worker (verifies isolation, ops acknowledges). Modes: automatic; Manual override (justified, small steps); Reduced-capacity; Storm Intake Mode (more sampling). Reqs: analyzer loss -> hold safe dose plus grabs; field

New part:
S118: When Storm Intake Mode is active, discretionary work is reviewed again because debris loading, chemical demand, and operator workload may change quickly.
S119: A Chlorine Residual Alarm during maintenance causes the affected task to pause until operations confirms whether the alarm is process-related or maintenance-induced.
S120: The Laboratory Technician supports work control by confirming sampling needs and by reporting any acceptance concern that could delay equipment return.
S121: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench remains available for maintenance-related samples when water quality confirmation is required before a unit is returned to service.
S122: Evidence for return to service may include local inspection results, functional test readings, instrument response checks, sample results, and operator acceptance comments.
S123: Equipment is returned to service only after temporary jumpers, bypasses, tools, spare parts, and barriers have been removed or formally accepted for continued use.
S124: If a post-maintenance test fails, the work order stays open and the Chief Operator determines whether the equipment remains isolated or can be operated under restriction.
S125: The SCADA Historian Server retains operating data needed to compare pre-work and post-work performance for pumps, dosing systems, filters, and level controls.
S126: Following maintenance closeout, disinfection control is returned to normal service only after the Chief Operator confirms that the chlorine feed controls, residual instruments, and level indications are responding consistently in the SCADA Historian Server.
S127: The Chlorine Contact Basin is operated to maintain the required contact time under the current production rate, basin level, and measured disinfectant residual.
S128: Operators adjust chlorine feed gradually so that changes in residual do not outrun mixing and contact time through the Chlorine Contact Basin.
S129: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm occurs, the control room verifies analyzer sample flow, compares the reading with a grab sample result, and holds any planned production increase until the condition is understood.
S130: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmatory residual results when analyzer drift, sample line fouling, or an unexpected residual trend is suspected.
S131: The Clearwell Level Controller maintains normal storage within established operating limits that protect disinfectant contact, reserve volume, and high-service pump suction conditions.
S132: Low clearwell level interlocks are configured to prevent pump operation from drawing the storage volume below the minimum level needed for safe hydraulic operation.
S133: High clearwell level alarms give operators time to reduce production or adjust downstream pumping before overflow conditions develop.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
